page: OVHcloud t1-le-45 is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance belonging to the Cloud GPU family, provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon Silver 4214 x86_64 processor operating at 3.0 GHz, offering 8 dedicated physical CPU cores without hyperthreading. Memory is configured at 45.0 GB of RAM, equating to 5.62 GB per dedicated core. Dedicated hardware acceleration is supplied by a single NVIDIA Volta V100 GPU equipped with 16 GB of VRAM. Bundled local storage includes a 300 GB NVMe SSD, and the baseline network connection is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations highlight clear distinctions between host CPU and accelerator capabilities. Single-core processing metrics, such as Geekbench single-core (1133.0) and stress-ng single-core (1251.85), register in the lower 25 percent tier. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a PassMark CPU score of 10212.67 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5385.0. In contrast, the NVIDIA V100 yields top-tier performance for deep learning tasks, achieving 1316.79 tokens per second for prompt ingestion and 117.97 tokens per second for text generation when running medium-sized 7B parameter models.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, pairing an older Intel Xeon Silver host processor with a high-bandwidth Volta V100 GPU delivers targeted computational acceleration without the expense of higher-tier host CPU architectures. Tradeoffs include modest single-thread CPU performance and limited baseline network bandwidth at 2 Gbps. The instance is suited for machine learning inference, small-to-medium model fine-tuning, computer vision workloads, and GPU-accelerated batch data processing.
description: OVHcloud t1-le-45 is a GPU-accelerated virtual server designed for accelerated computing workloads. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Silver 4214 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz, it provides 8 dedicated physical cores, 45.0 GB of system RAM, and 300 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Acceleration is handled by an onboard NVIDIA Volta V100 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. While single-thread CPU benchmark results place the system in the lower tiers, the GPU achieves top-tier results in medium 7B model LLM prompt processing and text generation. Baseline network throughput is configured at 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. This configuration provides a cost-effective hardware balance for machine learning inference, small-model deep learning tasks, and parallel compute pipelines that do not depend heavily on single-core host throughput.
